strengths.title: Proficient Python development
strengths.why_it_matters: Core to building reliable backend services and writing clean, maintainable code.
strengths.evidence_quote: Python, Django, FastAPI, PostgreSQL, Docker, pytest, GitHub Actions, Redis, REST APIs

strengths.title: Expertise in FastAPI/Django REST APIs
strengths.why_it_matters: Directly matches the job’s need to design REST APIs and data models for new features.
strengths.evidence_quote: Designed REST APIs in Django REST Framework for a shipment tracking product

strengths.title: Strong PostgreSQL performance tuning
strengths.why_it_matters: Ensures the services you own stay fast and scalable, a key production responsibility.
strengths.evidence_quote: Optimised slow PostgreSQL queries with indexes, cutting p95 latency from 900 ms to 180 ms.

strengths.title: Docker containerisation and CI/CD pipelines
strengths.why_it_matters: Allows you to ship code reliably and keep services running smoothly in production.
strengths.evidence_quote: Containerised five services with Docker and set up GitHub Actions CI/CD pipelines with automated deploys.

strengths.title: Test‑driven development with pytest
strengths.why_it_matters: High test coverage reduces bugs and speeds up code reviews, aligning with the mentorship and quality expectations.
strengths.evidence_quote: Wrote pytest unit and integration tests and raised coverage from 45% to 85%.

questions: A query is slow. How do you investigate and improve its performance?
Can you walk us through the steps you took to reduce PostgreSQL p95 latency from 900 ms to 180 ms?
Explain the difference between authentication and authorization, and how you would secure a public REST API you built.
How do you design your APIs to handle failure when calling external partner services?
You have no documented experience with Kubernetes. How would you approach learning it quickly to support a new service deployment?
What considerations would you make when moving a Docker‑based service to AWS?
What is a Python decorator? Describe one you have used in a recent project.
How do you decide what to test with pytest versus what to rely on integration tests?
Tell me about a time you mentored a junior engineer through a difficult bug. What was the outcome?
Describe a situation where you had to take ownership of a production incident. How did you resolve it and what did you learn?

tasks: Read the introductory sections of the Kubernetes documentation (official site) to understand core concepts.
Watch a 30‑minute tutorial on deploying a simple FastAPI app to a local Kind cluster.
Create a mini‑project: containerise a FastAPI service, write a Helm chart, and deploy it locally.
Complete the AWS free tier “Getting Started” guide for EC2 and ECR.
Deploy the Docker image from yesterday to AWS Elastic Container Service (ECS) using the console.
Write a short README summarising the steps you took and any challenges faced.
Review OWASP Top Ten and note the items most relevant to REST APIs.
Draft a security checklist for a new API endpoint (auth, rate‑limiting, input validation).
Practice explaining your checklist out loud as if interviewing.
Read the PostgreSQL “Using EXPLAIN” and “Indexes” docs.
Re‑run EXPLAIN on a sample slow query and identify missing indexes.
Write a short blog‑style post describing the optimisation you performed for the shipment tracking product.
Prepare a 2‑minute story about raising pytest coverage from 45 % to 85 % (challenge, actions, results).
Create a cheat‑sheet of common pytest fixtures you use and why.
Run a quick pair‑programming session with a friend to explain your testing approach.
Select two STAR stories (mentoring & incident ownership) and write them on index cards.
Practice delivering each story in under 90 seconds, focusing on impact.
Review the Amazon Leadership Principles and map your stories to at least two principles.
Do a full‑length mock interview with a peer or coach covering all topic groups above.
Record the session, then watch it to note any filler words or unclear explanations.
Refine your answers based on feedback and finalize a one‑page cheat sheet for the real interview.
